excerpt.before:
he Company conducts business in virtually all countries of the world with the primary focus on products related to human health and well-being. 

 The Company is organized into two business segments: Innovative Medicine and MedTech. The Innovative Medicine segment is focused on the following therapeutic areas: Oncology, Immunology, Neuroscience, Pulmonary Hypertension, Infectious Diseases, and Cardiovascular and Metabolism. Products in this segment are distributed directly to retailers, wholesalers, distributors, hospitals and healthcare professionals for prescription use. The MedTech segment includes a broad portfolio of products used in the Surgery, Orthopaedic, Cardiovascular and Vision fields. These products are distributed to wholesalers, hospitals and retailers, and used principally in the professional fields by physicians, nurses, hospitals, eye care professionals and clinics.

comment_letters.staff_ask: Staff asked J&J to disclose the material terms of the Genmab license for Darzalex and Darzalex Faspro (aggregate paid, royalty rate range, term and termination) and to file the agreement as an exhibit.
comment_letters.company_answer: J&J said the license is ordinary course and need not be filed, but agreed to add the 12%-20% royalty range and annual royalty paid (about $2B in 2024) to future 10-Ks.
comment_letters.next_filing_disclosure: FY2025 10-K Item 1 now states: Darzalex franchise 15.0% of revenue; royalty 12% to 20% of total Darzalex net sales; royalties to Genmab ~$2.4B (2025) and ~$2.0B (2024); Genmab patent families expire US 2029, EU 2031/2032. Agreement still not filed as an exhibit.
comment_letters.why_it_matters: A royalty of up to 20% on J&J's largest product (about $2.4B a year) was disclosed only because the SEC asked; it is a margin lever tied to 2029 patent expiry that the segment tables never showed.
comment_letters.impact_estimate: ~$2.4B royalty paid FY2025 (10-K); implied Darzalex sales ~$14B+ at 15.0% of revenue; royalty stops on the Genmab families after US 2029 expiry if J&J's own Faspro patents hold.
